title: Canada Pledges $560 Million to Brazil-Led Fund to Protect Rainforests
summary:
Canada has pledged up to $560 million over four years to help protect rainforests around the world. Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the commitment during a meeting with Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on Sunday in Manila, in the Philippines, during an ASEAN summit. The money will go to the Tropical Forests Forever Facility, a fund co-led by Brazil and Norway. The facility was launched at the COP30 climate summit in Brazil last year. It aims to grow to $125 billion, with about $100 billion coming from private-sector investors. The fund would support forest conservation in more than 70 countries, aiming to protect more than one billion hectares of tropical forest each year. Payments to countries would be tied to verified results, and at least 20 percent would go to Indigenous people and local communities.

The pledge is part of a $6-billion fund Canada promised this spring for international climate finance. It is also part of Canada's broader promise to provide more than $13 billion in climate finance to developing countries by 2031. Canada said the contribution would help the fund reach the fundraising targets needed to begin operations and attract more public and private investment.

'Canadians have always understood our responsibility to protect nature, both in our own backyard and around the world,' Carney said in a statement. He said protecting tropical forests is essential to halting biodiversity loss, stabilizing the climate, and safeguarding communities. Through an interpreter, Lula described the money as investments that will yield a profit, not 'donations, money for free.' The pledge comes as Carney has faced criticism from some environmental advocates and opposition parties over his government's rollback of some environmental policies. He has also faced criticism for not attending the last two UN climate summits.
why_it_matters: Rainforests store carbon and shelter countless species, so paying countries to keep them standing is one of the fastest ways to slow climate change and protect wildlife. The deal also tests whether rich countries will put real money behind their climate promises.

background_read: Tropical rainforests are thick forests near the equator that hold a huge share of the world's plants and animals, and they help steady the climate by storing carbon.
Many rainforests are being cut down for farming, logging, and building, which threatens wildlife and the people who live there.
The Tropical Forests Forever Facility is a fund that pays countries to keep their forests standing, with payments tied to proven results.
Countries meet at big climate summits to make promises like this one, where leaders agree to work together on protecting nature.
